title: Breathless but the Chest Is Normal / Say Normal, Then Look Beyond the Lungs

blocks.text: Breathless but the Chest Is Normal / Say Normal, Then Look Beyond the Lungs

AMaC MRCP PACES · R2-06 · Physical examination · PACES Station 1, respiratory examination · Skills A, B, D, E, G · 10 minutes (up to 6 minutes examining, then at least 4 minutes of examiner questions) · Guidelines: NICE NG106 Chronic heart failure in adults: diagnosis and management (published 12 September 2018; last updated 3 September 2025); NICE NG245 Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and chronic asthma management (published 27 November 2024) · Related AMaC: Cardiovascular examination: a soft flow murmur in a well young woman (R3-13)
Mr Tobias Fenwick is 41 and works as an IT technician. He has had six weeks of breathlessness on exertion. Please examine his respiratory system.
You may examine for up to 6 minutes. The examiners will then ask you questions.

sections.heading: 4. The Hook and the Examiner Trap

blocks.text: The Hook. A normal chest is a finding. Say "normal" without hedging, then widen the search to anaemia, the heart, the thyroid and anxiety.

The Examiner Trap. Candidates hunt for a sign and invent one: a wheeze, a crackle, clubbing. Pass: name each normal sign, then give the non-respiratory causes and tests. Fail: an invented sign, or "it is anxiety" with no tests.

rows: He looks well, so examine completely and quickly: do not search for something to find.
"May I examine your chest? Does anything hurt? Is this angle comfortable?"
Clean hands; introduce, consent; sit him at 45 degrees; hands, face, eyes, neck, then the chest.
Report what is there and what is not: normal expansion, resonant percussion, vesicular breathing.
"I'm going to tap and listen on both sides from the back. Please say 'ninety-nine'."
Expansion; percussion; auscultation; vocal resonance; nodes; JVP; ankles; cover him; clean hands.
Normal is a finding: say it plainly, then widen the search beyond the lungs.
"The respiratory examination is normal. I'd look for anaemia, heart or thyroid disease and anxiety."
Present in order; normal findings; differential; tests; safety net; thank him.
Starts without consent; rushes the deep breaths; leaves him exposed.
Cleans hands, introduces self, consents, asks about pain, sits him at 45 degrees, covers him afterwards.
Also offers a chaperone, keeps exposure to the minimum, and allows rests between deep breaths.
Disorganised; omits the hands, face or one side of the chest.
Hands, face, eyes, neck, then expansion, percussion and auscultation from the back, comparing sides.
Also checks the nodes, JVP and ankles.
Reports a wheeze, crackles or clubbing that are not present.
States expansion, percussion and breath sounds are normal, with no clubbing, cyanosis, nodes or oedema.
Also states normal JVP and heart sounds, and says a normal chest does not exclude asthma.
Names a lung disease with no signs to support it.
Says the chest is normal, and the breathlessness may come from anaemia, heart disease, thyroid disease, anxiety or poor fitness.
Also lists asthma, obesity and pulmonary vascular disease, with the test for each.
Spirometry, full blood count, thyroid function, ECG and chest X-ray.
Also adds FeNO if asthma is suspected, and NT-proBNP if heart failure is suspected, with echocardiography guided by the result (NG245, NG106).
Says it is all anxiety, with no tests or safety net.
Advises urgent review for chest pain, fainting, coughing blood or a swollen painful leg.
Also says to return if he becomes breathless lying flat, and gives a follow-up plan.

blocks.text: High-performance is an AMaC teaching label, not an official grade. It shows what lifts a pass from adequate to convincing.
Not used for this station type.

Findings, released as each step is done: slim, comfortable at rest; respiratory rate 14; pulse 72 regular; blood pressure 124/76; SpO2 98% on air; temperature 36.7 °C. Hands: no clubbing, no pallor. Eyes: conjunctivae pink. Neck: no nodes, no goitre; JVP not raised. Chest: trachea central; expansion normal and symmetrical; percussion resonant; vesicular breath sounds; no wheeze or crackles. Heart sounds normal. No ankle oedema.

Question ladder: 1. What do you find? (B, R3) A normal respiratory examination. 2. Why might he be breathless? (D, R4) Anaemia, heart disease, thyroid disease, anxiety, poor fitness; asthma needs objective tests (blood eosinophils or FeNO, then spirometry with bronchodilator reversibility). 3. What would you do? (E, R5) Spirometry, full blood count, thyroid function, ECG, chest X-ray; NT-proBNP if heart failure is suspected. 4. What would worry you? (E, R6) Chest pain, fainting, haemoptysis, a swollen painful leg, or breathlessness lying flat.

Curveballs: His mother died of heart failure at 50: cardiac causes move up; ECG and NT-proBNP. He is breathless only on stairs and worse when anxious: still test, do not assume. Your examination is normal; would you stop? No; test.
Cleans hands, introduces self, gains consent and offers rests between breaths (G)
Examines hands, face, eyes and neck before the chest (A)
Compares both sides from the back (A)
States expansion, percussion and breath sounds are normal (B)
States no clubbing, cyanosis, nodes or oedema without inventing signs (B)
Says the chest is normal and gives non-respiratory causes (D)
Requests spirometry, blood count, thyroid function, ECG and chest X-ray (E)
Gives a safety net for chest pain, fainting, haemoptysis and a swollen leg (E)
Covers him, cleans hands and thanks him (G)
Fail performance
CANDIDATE: Sit back. [R1 Fail]
CANDIDATE: (Listens at the front, then the back, but not the hands.) [R2 Fail] There is a faint wheeze. [R3 Fail] It's asthma. [R4 Fail]
EXAMINER: Plan?
CANDIDATE: Chest X-ray. [R5 Fail] It's probably anxiety. [R6 Fail]
Examiner note: No consent, a sign invented, a lung diagnosis with no support, only a chest X-ray, and anxiety offered without a safety net.
Pass performance
CANDIDATE: (Cleans hands.) Mr Fenwick, I'm one of the doctors. May I examine your chest? Does anything hurt? Is this angle comfortable? [R1 Pass]
CANDIDATE: (Hands, face, eyes, neck; expansion, percussion and auscultation from the back, comparing sides.) [R2 Pass]
CANDIDATE: Expansion, percussion and breath sounds are normal. There is no clubbing, cyanosis, nodes or oedema. [R3 Pass]
CANDIDATE: (Covers him, cleans hands.) Thank you. [R1 Pass]
EXAMINER: Diagnosis?
CANDIDATE: The chest is normal. His breathlessness may be from anaemia, heart disease, thyroid disease, anxiety or poor fitness. [R4 Pass]
EXAMINER: Tests?
CANDIDATE: Spirometry, full blood count, thyroid function, ECG and chest X-ray. [R5 Pass]
EXAMINER: Advice?
CANDIDATE: Seek urgent review for chest pain, fainting, coughing blood or a swollen painful leg. [R6 Pass]
Examiner note: Safe and complete. Did not state the normal heart signs, the other causes, the heart failure test or a follow-up plan.
High-performance performance
CANDIDATE: (Cleans hands.) Mr Fenwick, may I examine your chest? Would you like a chaperone? Rest between deep breaths if you need to. I'll keep you covered. [R1 High]
CANDIDATE: (Hands, face, eyes, neck, nodes, JVP; both sides from the back; ankles.) [R2 High]

CANDIDATE: A normal respiratory examination: normal expansion, percussion and breath sounds; normal JVP and heart sounds; no clubbing, cyanosis, nodes or oedema. A normal chest does not exclude asthma. [R3 High]
CANDIDATE: (Covers him, cleans hands, thanks him.) [R1 High]
EXAMINER: Diagnosis?

CANDIDATE: Normal chest. Anaemia (blood count), heart disease (ECG), thyroid disease (thyroid function), asthma (eosinophils or FeNO, then spirometry), obesity, pulmonary vascular disease and anxiety. [R4 High]
EXAMINER: Tests?

CANDIDATE: Spirometry with FeNO, blood count including eosinophils, thyroid function, ECG and chest X-ray; NT-proBNP if heart failure is suspected, then echocardiography as the result directs. [R5 High]
EXAMINER: Advice?
CANDIDATE: Urgent review for chest pain, fainting, coughing blood or a swollen painful leg, or if he is breathless lying flat. I'd see him again with the results. [R6 High]
Examiner note: Added the chaperone and rests, the nodes, JVP and ankles, normal heart signs, a test for each cause, NT-proBNP and a follow-up plan.
R3: Inventing a sign. Reporting a wheeze or crackle in a normal chest tells the examiners the candidate sees what they expect, not what is there.
R4: Naming a lung disease. Without signs it has no support, and the real causes outside the chest are never considered.
R5: Chest X-ray only. It cannot find anaemia, thyroid disease, heart disease or asthma.
R6: Offering anxiety with no safety net. Breathlessness has serious causes, and he is sent away with nothing to watch for.
"Let me compare both sides again before I go on."
"I find no abnormality, so I'd say the chest is normal."
"May I summarise what I found and give my diagnosis?"

Exertional breathlessness with a normal chest has causes outside the lungs: anaemia, heart disease, thyroid disease, anxiety, obesity and poor fitness. A normal examination does not exclude asthma: NICE NG245 advises a blood eosinophil count or FeNO first, then spirometry with bronchodilator reversibility if asthma is not yet confirmed.

If heart failure is suspected, NICE advises an NT-proBNP test. Above 2,000 ng/litre: specialist assessment and echocardiography within 2 weeks; 400 to 2,000 ng/litre: within 6 weeks; below 400 ng/litre: look for another cause (NG106, last updated 3 September 2025).
THINK: Normal chest: look beyond the lungs.
SAY: "The respiratory examination is normal."
DO: Complete, quick, no invented signs.
NUMBERS: NT-proBNP above 2,000 ng/litre: echo within 2 weeks; 400 to 2,000: within 6 weeks (NICE NG106, last updated 3 September 2025).
TRAP: Inventing a wheeze or crackle.
FINISH: Tests for each cause; chest pain, fainting, haemoptysis, swollen leg.

NICE NG106. Chronic heart failure in adults: diagnosis and management (published 12 September 2018; last updated 3 September 2025). https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng106 Supports: NT-proBNP testing, and echocardiography within 2 weeks (NT-proBNP above 2,000 ng/litre) or 6 weeks (400 to 2,000 ng/litre).

NICE NG245. Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and chronic asthma management (published 27 November 2024). https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng245 Supports: objective testing for asthma (eosinophil count or FeNO, then bronchodilator reversibility with spirometry); a normal examination does not exclude it.
